transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. 

Well, I'm here today because... I just feel like I’m always up and moving around. It's like even on a quiet day at home, I’m just bouncing from one thing to another. I'll go from working on my garden club list, over to my knitting bag, and then I'm looking through travel papers... all before I’ve really finished any one of those things. I just can't seem to settle down.
Have there been periods in your life where your energy and mood were so high that you felt like a completely different person, or that you were practically unstoppable?

No, I don't think I've ever felt quite like that. I mean, I've never felt unstoppable or like a completely different person. 

It's not really a... a high mood or anything like that. It's more just that constant feeling of needing to move around that I mentioned. Just regular me, just having a hard time staying put.
Looking back at your childhood, say in elementary school, was it difficult for you to sit still or focus on your schoolwork for long periods of time?

Yes, actually. Even back in grade school, it was a problem. My teachers used to tell my mother that I was a bright girl, but just... scattered. I was always losing my papers and talking out of turn. And I remember I was always wiggling in my seat, usually before I even finished my schoolwork. So, yes, it's been hard to sit still for a very long time.
Does this difficulty with staying focused or sitting still happen in most areas of your life, such as at work or when you are out with friends, or is it mostly just when you are at home?

It happens pretty much everywhere, not just at home. It’s actually started causing some real strain for me lately. At home with my husband, and... well, over at the community center too. The other volunteers there, and my husband, they just can't really count on me to keep plans straight without someone checking behind me. So, yes, it definitely affects me when I'm out doing things, too.
When you are working on your projects or tasks, do you often make careless mistakes because you are rushing or not paying close attention to the details?

Yes, I do. It happens quite a bit, actually. Like when I help out with the paperwork at the community center... I'll just completely miss a name on the sign-up sheet. Or I'll write down the wrong time for a room reservation on a note. And the frustrating part is, I always think I've checked it over, but then the mistakes are still there. I just... I miss those little details.
Do you often find yourself forgetting things like appointments, errands, or where you put your keys or phone throughout the day?

Yes, I do. I'll fully mean to call someone back, or pick up something from the store for supper, or write down an appointment on the calendar... and then it just completely slips away from me. It goes right out of my head until my husband asks me about it later.
Between your struggle to sit still and your difficulty with focus and organization, which would you say has been more of a constant, pervasive problem for you throughout your life?

I'm not really sure how to answer that, to be honest. I haven't really thought about which one is worse. It feels like they've both just... always been there, my whole life. I couldn't really say if the trouble sitting still has been more of a constant problem than losing my focus. They just both seem to happen.

If you had to describe your day-to-day life, would you say that you are bothered more by the constant urge to be physically moving, or by the frustration of not being able to keep your thoughts and tasks organized?

I really couldn't pick one over the other. They both bother me about the same amount. It's just... well, it's just how my days go. I'm always fidgeting or needing to get up, and I'm always misplacing things or losing my train of thought. Neither one really stands out as being more frustrating than the other, they're just both things I deal with all the time.

When you are in situations where you are expected to remain seated, such as at a movie theater, a religious service, or a long meeting, do you find it extremely difficult to stay in your seat for the duration?

No, not really. I mean... I can sit through church or a movie alright. I might shift around in my chair or mess with my purse a bit, but I don't find it extremely hard to actually stay in my seat. I haven't really noticed having to get up and leave or anything like that.
When you are in situations like a long meeting or a social gathering, do you find yourself talking excessively or frequently interrupting others while they are speaking?

No, I wouldn't say I do that. I mean, I like to talk, but I don't think I talk too much or interrupt people. I usually just listen and wait my turn if someone else is speaking. I haven't had anyone complain about me doing that, anyway.
Looking back at your life, would you say that you have experienced more symptoms related to being inattentive and disorganized, or more symptoms related to being physically restless and fidgety?

Well, honestly, it's a lot like what I mentioned a minute ago. Looking back over the years, I really don't think one stands out more than the other. I've always been a bit scatterbrained and disorganized, and I've always been the type to fidget or keep my hands busy. I'm not really sure I could pick one over the other... they've just both always been a part of how I am, about equal, I'd say.
